warnings: DEVELOPMENT RUN: two-layer (layer3.0.downsample.0, layer4.1.conv2). These numbers validate the implementation, not any architecture ranking. Layer selection is in the path and in `identity.layers`.
approximations: Interconnect energy uses Timeloop's Legacy network model with one shared 45nm wire constant and per-architecture switching terms (archs/_shared/noc.yaml); hop distance is derived by Timeloop from each level's Accelergy area. The recon arm scales the WEIGHT share of NoC energy by K/N like the other on-chip categories.
exact stored codeword count x measured DRAM refetch factor; parity + message padding; rounded up to whole DRAM words once

External parity is billed at the measured per-access energy of a DRAM weight read on this architecture, not at an independently modelled parity-region access cost. That is exact if parity is read from the same DRAM by the same controller, which is the conventional-ECC assumption.

complete codeword read: every bit of every DRAM weight read that Timeloop counts is billed, message and embedded parity alike, and no K/N reduction is applied at DRAM; no external parity; physical DRAM words are ESTIMATED as bits / word rounded up once at the end (bit-proportional -- Timeloop bills per 8-bit scalar); the final chunk's tail padding is reported, not charged, as for the baseline

ECC codec (decode/correction) energy is OUTSIDE this comparison: it is charged to neither arm (Task 2: do not silently change ECC codec energy). Note that the arms would decode different numbers of codewords -- the baseline packs whole weights into a separately stored codeword, the embedded layout cuts the weight bit stream itself -- so a codec cost would not cancel; it is simply not costed until a characterised codec energy is adopted. ECC_DECODE affects the sweep figures only.
This is a fixed-mapping, DRAM-only comparison. It credits no on-chip saving to the embedded arm and makes no inference-accuracy claim about overwriting weight LSBs with parity.

layout.layout_meaning: the MSB-first weight bit stream is cut into fixed n-bit codewords; weights straddle codeword boundaries; the parity overwrites the lowest-significance positions; storage is weight_bits per weight with no external parity

parity_significance.rule: per chunk, the n-k parity bits overwrite the positions of lowest bit significance (ties: higher chunk index first)

layout_source.pipeline: ECC-CODE-Engine/4-EmbeddingECC/ecc_embed.py -- approach `replace`, chunk_size = message_parity_size (the codeword n); one int8 tensor per call
layout_source.slicing: Input_Embedding/3-Testing/utils/messageSliceBasedOnChunkSize.py -- fixed n-bit chunks over the MSB-first 8-bit weight stream; chunks span weights; only the last chunk is zero-padded
layout_source.encoding: Input_Embedding/3-Testing/implementations/ParityOverwriteByTopWeightsEncode.py -- systematic BCH(n,k) via galois.BCH(n,k).G; the k highest-significance chunk positions are the message, the n-k lowest-significance positions are overwritten with the parity
layout_source.phases: Input_Embedding/3-Testing/implementations/secded_vectorized.py -- the chunk/weight alignment repeats every lcm(n, 8)/n chunks

DRAM.quote: study-wide DRAM model, not from the paper

iact_glb + psum_glb.modelled: 72 kB iact (48 banks) + 120 kB psum (64 banks) = 192 kB

weights_glb.modelled: !Nothing -- weights have no GLB level in v2
weights_glb.rationale: Weights stream from DRAM through the weight routers into the PE spads. This is the single largest architectural difference from v1 in a weight-traffic study, so it is left as the paper describes it. The eyeriss_v2_like_wglb variant exists to bound what that costs.

weights_spad.quote: Table IV: weight data: 288B (SRAM); Fig. 17: 96 x 24b SRAM
weights_spad.modelled: depth 96, width 24, datawidth 8 -> 288 weights/PE, 55,296 on chip
weights_spad.contested: Sec. III-D ("each count-data pair is 12b and is stored in a 12b word of the data SPad") supports a CSC-native reading of 2 weights per 24b word = 192 weights/PE. The dense-bytes rule in standard.yaml gives 288. The difference is a third of v2's on-chip weight capacity and therefore materially changes its DRAM refetch; it is the largest single modelling judgement in the study. Recorded here so a reader can disagree with it.

ifmap_spad.quote: Table IV: iact data: 24B (Reg); Fig. 17: 16 x 12b Regs
ifmap_spad.approximation: Timeloop requires width % datawidth == 0 and the published word is 12b, which 8 does not divide. Modelled as 24 x 8b: same 24 B, same 24 operands, 24 narrow words instead of 16 wide ones. Per-access register energy is therefore for a narrower word than the design has. This is the only place in the study where a published word width cannot be declared as-is.

psum_spad.quote: Table IV: psum: 80B (Reg); Fig. 17: 32 x 20b Regs

mapper.seed_note: timeloop-mapper v4 exposes no random seed; pytimeloop's Mapper spec has no `random_seed` attribute. ECC_MAPPER_SEED is RECORDED so a result says which value was asked for, but it does not make the search deterministic. What does bound it is the thread count and victory condition, both of which are in the fingerprint -- so pin ECC_MAPPER_THREADS for a reproducible run rather than leaving it at 'all cores', which differs per machine.
